summary: One focused behavior within the leaf limits: the tier-2 useful/neutral fauna tier (4-6 roster-selected species) behaves per its private-roster signature rules in the headless production simulation, with at least 2 species mechanically beneficial. The per-species signature rules are content instances of this single behavior batch - the roster tier is sized and selected upstream by WI-01b, not open-ended - and the 2+ friendly floor is an acceptance facet of AC-roster-behavior owned here, with final AC-roster-behavior proof remaining with WI-03c per the ST-03 plan. Changed subsystems are exactly three concrete owners: world content data (CreatureDefs in src/content/secret/), creature simulation (src/sim/Simulation.ts), and headless scenario tests (harness src/sim/scenario.ts); both framework files verified to exist as production code with real resource/interaction rules (harvest/interact, inventory), which grounds the friendly-interaction assumption, and the stated escape hatch (minimal meter/rule per section 30) stays inside those subsystems. Boundaries are clean and non-overlapping: no production spawns and no renderer work (WI-03b2, which correctly depends_on WI-03b1), no predators (WI-03c), no large/colossal staging (WI-03d). AC-roster-behavior and AC-roster-tests are retained verbatim from WI-03b; their union with WI-03b2's AC-roster-count and AC-roster-tests covers all three parent criteria. depends_on: [] is correct - ST-01/ST-02 ancestor dependencies are inherited through ST-03 and documented in both story plans, so no direct dependency is required. Verification is focused headless evidence: per-species signature-rule scenarios through the production simulation (including the second-behavior trigger-timing check and the dangerous-looking-safe never-harms check), the 2+ friendly floor check, and tier-2 spoiler containment (roster-wide audit deferred to WI-03d). The fresh-session handoff (WI-03b/plan.md, numbered request sections, WI-01b's design_private/creature_candidates.md artifact, section 46 quality bar, spoiler rules) lets a fresh implementer proceed without reconstructing the project. Matches exactly the leaf shape the parent's split receipt prescribed.
